doc.brief: A `GtkGesture` subclass optimized for singe-touch and mouse gestures.
doc.md:
A `GtkGesture` subclass optimized for singe-touch and mouse gestures.

Under interaction, these gestures stick to the first interacting sequence,
which is accessible through [`GestureSingle.get_current_sequence()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GestureSingle#method:get_current_sequence)
while the gesture is being interacted with.

By default gestures react to both %GDK_BUTTON_PRIMARY and touch events.
[`GestureSingle.set_touch_only()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GestureSingle#method:set_touch_only) can be used to change the
touch behavior. Callers may also specify a different mouse button number
to interact with through [`GestureSingle.set_button()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GestureSingle#method:set_button), or react
to any mouse button by setting it to 0. While the gesture is active, the
button being currently pressed can be known through
[`GestureSingle.get_current_button()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GestureSingle#method:get_current_button).

get_button.brief: Returns the button number `gesture` listens for.
get_button.md:
Returns the button number `gesture` listens for.

If this is 0, the gesture reacts to any button press.

get_current_button.brief: Returns the button number currently interacting with `gesture`, or 0 if there is none.
get_current_button.md:
Returns the button number currently interacting
with `gesture`, or 0 if there is none.

get_current_sequence.brief: Returns the event sequence currently interacting with `gesture`.
get_current_sequence.md:
Returns the event sequence currently interacting with `gesture`.

This is only meaningful if [`Gesture.is_active()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Gesture#method:is_active)
returns `TRUE`.

get_exclusive.brief: Gets whether a gesture is exclusive.
get_exclusive.md:
Gets whether a gesture is exclusive.

For more information, see [`GestureSingle.set_exclusive()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.GestureSingle#method:set_exclusive).

get_touch_only.brief: Returns `TRUE` if the gesture is only triggered by touch events.
get_touch_only.md: Returns `TRUE` if the gesture is only triggered by touch events.

set_button.brief: Sets the button number `gesture` listens to.
set_button.md:
Sets the button number `gesture` listens to.

If non-0, every button press from a different button
number will be ignored. Touch events implicitly match
with button 1.

set_exclusive.md:
Sets whether `gesture` is exclusive.

An exclusive gesture will only handle pointer and "pointer emulated"
touch events, so at any given time, there is only one sequence able
to interact with those.

set_touch_only.brief: Sets whether to handle only touch events.
set_touch_only.md:
Sets whether to handle only touch events.

If `touch_only` is `TRUE`, `gesture` will only handle events of type
%GDK_TOUCH_BEGIN, %GDK_TOUCH_UPDATE or %GDK_TOUCH_END. If `FALSE`,
mouse events will be handled too.

button.brief: Mouse button number to listen to, or 0 to listen for any button.
button.md: Mouse button number to listen to, or 0 to listen for any button.

exclusive.md:
Whether the gesture is exclusive.

Exclusive gestures only listen to pointer and pointer emulated events.

touch-only.brief: Whether the gesture handles only touch events.
touch-only.md: Whether the gesture handles only touch events.
